canada.title: It started with a lobster dinner. Now it's an East Coast institution
canada.summary: The Shore Club in Hubbards, N.S., has spent more than eight decades serving up classic lobster suppers and live music to people from around the globe. A new CBC documentary pulls back the curtain on how the Harnish family managed to turn a rural dance hall into a Maritime institution.

canada.title: Less than half of Crown-owned heritage buildings are in fair or better condition
canada.summary: Forty-five per cent of Crown-owned heritage buildings are in fair or better condition, says a federal government report.

canada.title: Crown can't prove he pulled the trigger, but B.C. man guilty of 1st degree murder: Judge
canada.summary: A British Columbia man has been convicted of first-degree murder in a gangland slaying in Nanaimo, B.C., five years ago, even though the Crown couldn't prove he pulled the trigger.

canada.title: Holiday spirit alive in Saskatchewan despite warm weather, lack of snow
canada.summary: It's one of the warmest Novembers on record for Saskatchewan, but that's not stopping people from enjoying the festive season, with Santa Claus parades and holiday markets around the province.

canada.title: Paulatuk, N.W.T., looks to protect historical graveyard from shoreline erosion
canada.summary: Cape Parry used to be a home to Inuit in the 1950s and '60s who later moved to Paulatuk. Erosion is now threatening a small graveyard at the former settlement.

canada.title: Freshwater supply challenges threaten Canada's security, internal federal memo says
canada.summary: Pressures on the supply of fresh water pose challenges that will affect Canada’s “long-term security and prosperity” if left unaddressed, an internal government memo warns.

canada.title: B.C.'s 2021 heat dome killed hundreds. New research shows it could have been worse
canada.summary: New research shows 2021 wasn't the first time B.C. baked in a prolonged bout of intense heat.

canada.title: Football fans of all stripes gather in Calgary ahead of 113th Grey Cup
canada.summary: The Grey Cup Festival brought supporters of teams from across Canada to Calgary's Stampede Park, where festivities included live music performances, football-themed activations and rodeo shows ahead of the big game between the Edmonton Elks and Montreal Alouettes.

canada.title: A hobby that pops: Saskatoon man's massive Coca-Cola collection inspired by rural roots
canada.summary: Jon Aschenbrener of Saskatoon estimates he has 5,000 to 10,000 items in his collection of Coca-Cola memorabilia, which began on the family farm northeast of Cupar, Sask.

canada.title: Manitoba ski hill racing to make flood-damage repairs before opening for season
canada.summary: With debris from June's devastating flood at Asessippi Ski Resort still around, staff are up against the clock making sure the slopes are groomed and open in time for the holidays.

canada.title: Drop in Yukon lotteries revenue creates gap for sport and art groups that rely on funding
canada.summary: The Yukon Lotteries Commission helps to fund sports and art organizations across the territory and as residents move to online gambling, the organizations worry about a dip in support.

canada.title: Public can participate in air quality review of Saint John Irving plant
canada.summary: The public has 180 days to take part in the province’s public participation process for the renewal of an air quality approval for Irving Pulp and Paper’s Reversing Falls mill in Saint John.

canada.title: ‘We made this happen’: 2SLGBTQ+ groups celebrate federal budget funding
canada.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government released its 2026-27 budget on Nov. 5, unveiling $150 billion in spending. It includes $60 million over four years for 2SLGBTQ+ organizations across Canada, plus $15 million every year after.

canada.title: Free Halifax workshop offers youth writers a place to hone their craft
canada.summary: A new workshop by poet Sue Goyette is aimed at young writers. It's called FutureWords, and the free program gets youths engaged in creative writing exercises to develop their skills and hone their craft.

canada.title: Pre-teen entrepreneur hopes to piece together N.L.'s largest Lego store
canada.summary: Twelve-year-old William Pinsent of Gander, won the Youth Ventures Newfoundland and Labrador Environmentally Sustainable Venture Award and the Gander and Area Chamber of Commerce’s Young Entrepreneur Award last month for his Lego business, Newfound Bricks.

canada.title: Why researchers are using drones to keep polar bears and people apart
canada.summary: While studies have shown drone hazing to be effective on black bears, researchers are now trying to see if it works with polar bears — a bigger, more curious and more aggressive species. The goal is to adapt the technology to Canada's North and try to take some of the risk out of managing the bears.

bds.h: SpaceX’s Starship captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
bds.lede: SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.
rows: Video. SpaceX's Starship spacecraft was successfully caught by giant mechanical arms at its Texas launch tower after a 22-hour journey, marking the first successful midair capture of a Starship returning from space.
SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.
It was the first recovery of a Starship from orbit, a major milestone for a rocket SpaceX founder Elon Musk says will dramatically lower launch costs.
